chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Sayf ibn Amira, from his father, from Qutayba al-A'sha, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The merit of the beginning time over the end time is like the merit of the Hereafter over the world.

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: The world/this life — the present worldly existence, used here as a symbol of what is lesser in value
key_terms.الْآخِرَة: The Hereafter — the eternal realm after death, contrasted with al-dunya (the transient world)
key_terms.الْوَقْت الْأَوَّل: The first/beginning time — the earliest moment within a prayer's prescribed window, considered most meritorious
key_terms.فَضْل: Merit, virtue, excellence — used to convey the superiority of one thing over another in Islamic ethics

ai.seo_question: Why is praying at the beginning of prayer time better than praying at the end according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) draws a vivid analogy to emphasize the superiority of performing salat at the earliest moment of its prescribed time. Just as the eternal Hereafter transcends the transient world in every measure of worth, so too does praying at the first opportunity of the prayer time surpass delaying it. This teaching reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on al-waqt al-awwal (the preferred time) as an act of eager obedience and taqwa.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Salma Bin Al Khattab, from Ali Bin Sayf Bin Ameyra, from his father, from Quteyba Al A’ash, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The merit of the beginning time upon the end time is like the merit of the Hereafter over the world’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Salmah ibn al-Khattab from Ali ibn Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from his father from Qutaybah al-‘A’sha’ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The outstanding quality of the beginning of the time for Salah (prayer) is like the outstanding quality of the next life compared to the worldly life.’”
